newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends lower on buyer absence.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends lower on buyer absence.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower, extending the market's softness in the absence of buyers, traders said.
They said a weaker Tokyo market also pressured local prices.
"It's still very quiet. There's a few sellers out there but no buyers," said one local trader.
Trading was also restricted by a holiday in Thailand and ahead of the Moslem Eid al-Adha holiday on Friday.
Traders said they expected the market to come off further as rising stocks may force producers to lower their offer prices.
At the close, May RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 290.50 cents ($1.16) a kg, unchanged from Monday.
May SMR 20 buyer ended down a cent at 274 cents ($1.09).
Trading houses quoted SMR CV at 343 cents a kg, SMR L at 323, SMR 10 at 275 and drum latex at 233 FOB.
The INRO five-day moving average was 221.79 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on April 14 against 222.22 on April 11. The daily indicator price was 221.05 versus 221.03.
